answer: Delayed reputation bridge. A new identity's reputation accrues only after a fixed latency, and each identity must pay a recurring rent plus a per-message whisper fee that scales with its unproven age. Older, established identities get a thread of low-cost throughput; fresh ones pay steadily more until they either persist or exit. An attacker running N sybils pays N times rent and inflated fees every cycle, so duplication costs scale linearly while honest single identities amortize over time.
